title: Perfect tensor tests detect pseudo-coherence on a flat finitely presented scheme
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $p:X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be a separated, flat morphism of finite presentation [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-morphism-conventions, def-weil-flat-morphism]. Let $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category]. Suppose that for every perfect object $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-perfect-complex], the derived global sections $R\Gamma(X,E\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_X}K)$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image, def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure], viewed in the derived category of $R$-modules, are pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Then $K$ is pseudo-coherent on $X$ [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex]. There is no Noetherian hypothesis on $R$ and no properness hypothesis on $p$.

source.place: Tag 0GES, lemma-characterize-pseudo-coh-improved; Tag 09UU, lemma-check-relative-pseudo-coherence-on-charts, applied with the identity closed immersion X -> X. Flatness and finite presentation convert relative pseudo-coherence into absolute pseudo-coherence.

proof.text: The affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Finite presentation of $p$ includes quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. Apply permanence under composition with the structure morphism of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ to conclude that $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. These are the scheme hypotheses needed in the next two steps.

source.place: Tag 0GES, lemma-characterize-pseudo-coh-improved: hypotheses for perfect.tex Tags 0GEN and 0CSH

proof.text: For every perfect $P$, the hypothesis makes $R\Gamma(X,P\otimes^L K)$ quasi-isomorphic to a bounded-above complex of finite free $R$-modules. Above the bound all terms, hence all cohomology modules, vanish. Thus each perfect tensor test has eventually vanishing cohomology. Apply the perfect-tensor upper-boundedness criterion on the qcqs scheme $X$ to obtain one integer $b$ with $\mathcal H^i(K)=0$ for $i>b$. The bound may initially depend on $P$; the criterion needs no uniform test bound.

source.place: Tag 0GES, lemma-characterize-pseudo-coh-improved, bounded-above reduction using perfect.tex Tag 0GEN

proof.text: Apply the perfect-to-pseudo-coherent tensor-test lemma with $A=R$, the upper bound from step 2, and the original perfect-test hypothesis. It gives that $R\Gamma(X,E\otimes^L K)$ is pseudo-coherent in $D(R)$ for every pseudo-coherent $E$. All its hypotheses hold: $X$ is qcqs by step 1 and $K$ has quasi-coherent cohomology by assumption. Now the pseudo-coherent-test relative criterion, using the separated finite-presentation morphism $p$, makes $K$ pseudo-coherent relative to $\operatorname{Spec}R$.

source.place: Tag 0GES, lemma-characterize-pseudo-coh-improved, using perfect.tex Tag 0CSH and Tag 0CSL, lemma-characterize-pseudo-coherent

proof.text: Use the flat-ambient chart criterion with $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $P=X$, and $i=\mathrm{id}_X$. The identity is a closed immersion: it is a homeomorphism onto the closed subset $X$ and the map on structure sheaves is the identity, hence surjective. The ambient map is exactly $p$, which is flat and locally of finite presentation by hypothesis. The criterion therefore makes $R(\mathrm{id}_X)_*K$ pseudo-coherent on $X$. Direct image under the identity is the identity functor, and its derived functor is again the identity (apply it to any resolution); thus this object is $K$. This proves the required absolute pseudo-coherence.
